memories.content: The user keeps waterproof shoes for rainy days to the left of the entrance.
On a day the user walked in the rain wearing thin shoes, their socks became wet and they changed them after arrival.
On the next rainy day, the user wore waterproof shoes and their feet remained dry.
On a day the user walked for a long time in new shoes, their heel chafed and they shortened the route home.
The user wore the same shoes on two short outings before using them on a long walk.
On a day the user dried an umbrella outside the entrance, they found it immediately before the next outing.
On a day the user put a folded wet umbrella in their bag, documents inside became wet.
When rain is forecast, the user's mother expects the user may forget an umbrella and sets out a spare at the entrance.
When proposing a long-distance walking plan, check both the weather that day and recent records of shoe discomfort.
Even if the local agent knows a shoe's location, it cannot know its current condition or whether it is usable.
The user collects clothes for donation in a large bag beside the entrance.
After emptying an entire drawer at once, the user could not find a charger they needed.
During the next organizing session, the user sorted items by type and put only items to be discarded in the bag.
Even after photographing unworn clothes, the user did not take them out again for one month.
After moving those clothes to the donation bag, the user cleared one closet compartment.
The user nearly discarded an important paper with advertising and checked the recycling box again.
During the next organizing session, the user kept a separate document box and did not mix the papers.
The user's mother asks the user to check whether she needs kitchen items in good condition before discarding them.
Confirm with the user before marking a personal document or another person's property as a disposal candidate.
The local agent cannot determine an object's emotional meaning from frequency of use alone.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: rainy-weather footwear and umbrella use on one side, and household sorting and disposal on the other. Each also records distinct family involvement, decision safeguards, and limits on what a local agent can infer; no claims overlap operationally or conflict.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers staged sorting, donation-driven decluttering, document separation, family consultation before disposal, confirmation for sensitive property, and uncertainty about emotional significance.
